To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nonverbal behavior is automatically sensed, extracted, and can be validly measured.
the applicant’s vocal nonverbal immediacies (turn duration, tempo variation) and gazing are validly extracted and best predict hiring decision.

the applicant’s vocal nonverbal behavior, as well as his or her visual nonverbal behavior is validly extracted via automated sensing and that vocal nonverbal immediateness behavior predicts recruiter hiring decision, whereas visual nonverbal immediate behavior does not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how nonverbal behavior in social interactions can be automatically recorded and extracted
the question how nonverbal behavior coding can be achieved via nonverbal social sensors.
the question of whether and what kind of applicant nonverbal cues, such as visual and vocal cues, can be extracted and whether these cues can be used to predict hiring decisions of recruiters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the automated extracted nonverbral cues are not only validly extracted but also can predict the recruiter hiring decision.
the results of the present study indicate that nonverbal social sensors can be used to record and extract nonverbal behavior with a certain degree of validity.
the nonverbal social behavior of job applicants can be validly recorded and extracted by using nonverbal social sensors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonverbal social behavior of the applicant can be automatically sensed and extracted in a valid manner.
we have illustrated that it is possible to extract nonverbal behavior automatically and that this extracted behavior can be valid.
nonverbal social behavior can be extracted via ubiquitous sensing and that the extracted nonverbal behavior is valid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nonverbal behavior of social interaction partners can be validly and reliably sensed and extracted.
nonverbal social behavior is validly extracted via nonverbal social sensors, which can be used in future nonverbal behavior research.
nonverbal social cues can be valid and reliably extracted via nonverbal social sensors.
